dataFields.name: Scope

dataFields.name: Payable days
dataFields.validation: Days the month's attendance makes payable, with off-days and holidays excluded (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Paid leave taken
dataFields.validation: Leave within the allowance, paid in full (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Unpaid days
dataFields.validation: Leave beyond the allowance, plus any day absent with no leave request. Each deducted at the daily rate (BR-4, BR-5).

dataFields.name: Daily rate
dataFields.validation: Derived from the salary in force for that month (BR-7).

dataFields.name: Deductions
dataFields.validation: Unpaid days at the daily rate, and any other deduction.

dataFields.name: Statutory contributions
dataFields.validation: Where they apply, from the statutory details on the record.

dataFields.name: Advance recovery
dataFields.validation: The instalment due this month against an outstanding advance (BR-8).

dataFields.name: Net pay
dataFields.validation: What the employee is actually paid.
dataFields.formula: net = gross − unpaid_days × daily_rate − statutory_contributions − advance_recovery

dataFields.name: Override reason

businessRules.rule: Pay is calculated from recorded attendance. Nobody types a salary figure into a run, because a typed figure is a figure nobody can trace to a day worked.
Accounts may generate for every working employee at once or for a single employee. A correction for one person does not require the whole month to be run again.
The month's attendance is read with the off-day calendar applied, so a day the school was closed is not counted against anybody.
Leave taken up to the allowance held on the staff record is paid. Every day beyond it is deducted at the daily rate — an employee allowed two paid leaves who takes three loses one day's salary.
A day absent with no leave request at all is treated as an unpaid day and deducted at the same daily rate.
Where an employee joins or leaves part-way through the month, pay is calculated for the days worked only, from the joining date, the leaving date or the contract end date held on the staff record.
The calculation works from the salary in force for the month being run, not the latest figure. A rise effective in August does not change what July was paid.
Any instalment due against an outstanding advance is recovered in the run and the advance balance falls by it.
The generated salaries are visible only to the Principal and Accounts. The School Admin starts the run but does not see the figures, per the visibility rule.
The Principal may override a figure or the approval itself, and every override is recorded against their name with a reason. An override nobody can trace is a payment nobody can defend.
Payment is released only after the run is approved, and the release posts to the ledger. A salary generated is not a salary paid.
Every approval in this module is configuration-based. The Super Admin sets which role performs each one, and the chain described here is the default.
A generated salary is never deleted. A wrong figure is corrected before approval, or adjusted afterwards, and both stay on the record.

basicFlow.userAction: Clicks Generate Salary for the payroll month.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Opens the run for the month without showing the School Admin any salary figure.

basicFlow.userAction: Chooses whether to generate for every working employee at once or for a single employee.

basicFlow.systemResponse: Pulls each employee's attendance for the month, applying the off-day calendar and the paid-leave allowance held on their staff record.
Calculates gross pay, deductions, statutory contributions and any advance recovery, from the salary in force for that month, and pro-rates a part month.
Stores the generated salary against the employee and the month, visible to the Principal and Accounts alone.

basicFlow.userAction: Overrides a figure or the approval itself where needed.

alternateFlows.condition: Only one employee needs a salary generated
alternateFlows.behaviour: The run covers that employee alone, so a correction for one person does not require the whole month again (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: The employee took more leave than their allowance
alternateFlows.behaviour: Leave up to the allowance is paid and every day beyond it is deducted at the daily rate. An employee allowed two who takes three loses one day (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: The employee joined or left part-way through the month
alternateFlows.behaviour: Pay is calculated for the days worked only, from the joining date, the leaving date or the contract end date on the record (BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: The employee has an outstanding advance
alternateFlows.behaviour: The instalment due is recovered in the run and the advance balance falls by it (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The Principal disagrees with a deduction
alternateFlows.behaviour: The figure is overridden with a reason and the override is recorded against their name, since a payment nobody can trace is a payment nobody can defend (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: An attendance error is found during review
alternateFlows.behaviour: The run is returned, the attendance correction goes through its own approval, and the run is regenerated rather than the figure being typed over.

departures.requirement: Every figure in a generated salary is calculated from attendance, leave and the salary in force. There is no field into which a pay amount can be typed, only an override which is recorded.
The run resolves the salary in force for the month being run, so a later rise never changes an earlier month.

Payroll runs, generated salaries and overrides are retained 7 years as financial records.

openQuestions.question: How is the daily rate derived — calendar days, working days, or a fixed divisor?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and the three give materially different deductions. Same open point as on salary.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
